articles.headline: Wolff braced for 'full-on fight' amid Verstappen resurgence
keyFacts: Toto Wolff said he expects a full-on fight at the front of Formula 1 into 2027 following Max Verstappen and Red Bull's resurgence.
Mercedes are closing on a world championship double, while Red Bull chase a third consecutive win at the United States Grand Prix.
Red Bull team boss Laurent Mekies stated the team's development focus has shifted to 2027 with no further substantial car upgrades planned.
body: F1: Toto Wolff says Max Verstappen, Red Bull resurgence adds to expectation of 'full-on fight' into 2027 season

Mercedes are fast closing on a world championship double, but Red Bull are threatening to end the 2026 season with F1's fastest car after back-to-back wins for Max Verstappen; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin from Friday evening, live on Sky Sports F1
Monday 19 October 2026 16:23, UK
Toto Wolff believes in-form Red Bull will be a central part of the "full-on fight" he is expecting at the front of the Formula 1 field into 2027.

Wolff's Mercedes team are closing in on a world championship double heading into the closing races of this season, with Kimi Antonelli able to clinch the drivers' title as early as this weekend's United States Grand Prix if results go his way.

The strength of Mercedes' challenge in both championship races was built on a flying start to the season - which has been the first of the sport's new regulation era - with eight wins from the campaign's first 10 rounds.
However, their win rate has slowed since then with three victories in the last seven, with Ferrari, McLaren and latterly Red Bull all showing ability to challenge the Silver Arrows on race weekends.

Red Bull, in particular, had started the season lagging behind the leading pace but Max Verstappen has now won the last two races, a turnaround in form which Mercedes chief Wolff has been impressed by.
"I really think that you need to take your hat off to what Red Bull has done this season," said Wolff after Verstappen's dominant victory in Singapore.
"How they have developed the car and how it's all come together as a package and then you put Max Verstappen in the car and he feels a thing that wants it to drive, then these are the results.

"By far the quickest guy [in Singapore], the quickest guy in Kuala Lumpur and let's see when our upgrade hopefully starts to work and land in a place where it should be, whether we can be competitive against him, but one thing is for sure, next year, it's a full-on fight between the teams and Red Bull is part of that."
Wolff also believes Red Bull's power unit, the first in their history, has been performing strongly.
"I haven't seen the data yet from Singapore, but you can't see that it's lagging," added Wolff.

"They have done it well. The ICE [Internal Combustion Unit] seems to be very competitive. Obviously, you can see that with the ADUO [ranking, which Red Bull have found to be leading] but also in terms of energy recovery and energy deployment, they're pretty good."
Will Red Bull sustain winning form to end of 2026?

Red Bull now head to Austin's Circuit of the Americas chasing a third win in succession this weekend as their late-season bid to overhaul McLaren for third in the Constructors' Championship continues.
Their RB22 car's performance and, crucially, stability was improved by a significant aerodynamic upgrade at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix last month.
That update did, however, represent the team's final one of note this season with their development focus now on their 2027 car.

With six rounds left, Red Bull team boss Laurent Mekies admits the recent "pecking order could very rapidly change if some or many of our competitors bring upgrades", although he says there is still much for them to learn and improve with their existing package.

Mekies added: "There will be no other substantial upgrade to the car. Don't get me wrong, it does not mean that we will not continue to push very hard to improve, continue to push very hard to use every remaining race to learn for this year and to learn for next year.
"That's what we have to say to each other. The first win is the target, but the other target is to take all the learning. So, the development programme will not change. We have put our focus to 2027.

"We think there is still a huge amount of learning in 2026 that we could use in 2027. I'd like to take the time to say a huge congrats to Pierre [Wache]'s team, to Ben [Hodgkinson]'s team, for the work at Milton Keynes they have done in order to be in that position to fight for the win on different tracks.

"As I said, even on a weekend where you take two poles and two wins like this [Singapore] weekend, we are still very honest with each other about the fact that there were still a number of things we would like to see better done, even on a weekend like here. That's the spirit of this team and with that spirit we will go and reset and tackle the next race."

articles.headline: Did Silent Hill: Townfall put you in the shoes of a workplace shooter?
keyFacts: Silent Hill: Townfall features a late-game chapter called Richard where players control a character navigating an energy company headquarters with a shotgun.
Destructoid reported that players discover the protagonist Richard is actually the company CEO whose negligence caused a fatal oil rig fire.
Destructoid stated that the enemies Richard hunts are the literal widows of workers who died in the disaster, reflecting his lack of remorse.
body: Silent Hill: Townfall is a harrowing ride from start to finish, but to me, the scariest moment comes near the end. It’s not scary because you face down some terrifying monster; it’s scary because you’re the monster, and you might not realize it on your first playthrough.
Major spoilers ahead. You have been warned.

Townfall’s penultimate chapter, “Richard,” puts you in control of the titular character, a mysterious figure who subtly guides the game’s protagonist, Simon, as he explores the Scottish town of St. Amelia. As a sort of flashback, the chapter takes place inside Chapman Energy Corp’s (the company at the center of the game’s story) headquarters, and you have to make your way to the CEO’s office on the top floor.

Things get grim as soon as you enter the building, with you soon discovering the halls are littered with the mangled corpses of “other” Richards who tried and failed to complete the mission you’re on now. However, the tone shifts almost immediately when you swipe a shotgun from one of the Richards and load it with the myriad of shells you find lying around.

From here, the CEG HQ starts to feel like a section from a completely different game. Monsters known as Widows soon appear, but instead of charging at you like the others you’ve encountered so far, they embrace stealth, crouching behind lockers or waiting around corners to ambush you. They can be dangerous if they get the drop on you, but a solid shotgun blast invariably takes them down.

Before long, the Widows stop being a threat and start being a nuisance. Once you learn how they work, you go on the offensive, using the building’s layout to corner them where they hide and fill them with buckshot before they can attack. Still, the moment doesn’t feel triumphant, and the reason is simple and horrifying: the monsters aren’t the threat here; you are.

Throughout Townfall , you slowly piece together that C.E.G., at the behest of its CEO, ignored safety protocols while installing new equipment on an oil rig off the coast of St. Amelia. Said equipment soon failed, triggering a catastrophic fire that claimed the lives of over a hundred people. In the aftermath, C.E.G.’s CEO did everything he could to cover his tracks, pretending nothing could have prevented the tragedy.
And just who is this greedy, cowardly CEO? You find out when Richards enters the CEO’s office and picks up his own ID card.

Once you realize Richard is C.E.G.’s CEO, small details you might have noticed throughout his chapter start clicking into place. The Widows Richard guns down are the literal widows of the workers who died because of his negligence. The fact that he only sees his own corpse piling up reflects the idea that, in his own entitled mind, Richard is the sole victim of the St. Amelia disaster, a “man of industry” being unjustly persecuted by an ungrateful town.

Richard, like so many people in corporate power today, chose profit over the people his company claimed to serve. And when the consequences of his choices become too big to hide, he chooses destruction over reflection, tearing through his workplace with a gun, mowing down the loved ones of the employees he let die in a desperate attempt to regain control.

Comparing Richard’s gameplay section to Simon and Rose’s only makes the flags redder. Simon and Rose’s gameplay sections subtly reinforce the characters’ remorse for their roles in the St. Amelia tragedy, encouraging you to avoid violence through resource scarcity and empathy-inducing monster design. Richard’s gameplay, in contrast, actively encourages you to mow down your foes, even awarding you an Achievement for killing thirty of them.

Through this haunting gameplay segment, Townfall seamlessly puts the player in the headspace of a man who caused immeasurable suffering and feels absolutely no guilt over it. And in my opinion, that makes it one of the scariest moments I’ve ever played in a video game.
The post Did Silent Hill: Townfall put you in the shoes of a workplace shooter? appeared first on Destructoid .

body: The Indianapolis Colts just lost to the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season. The 2-3 Colts drop to 2-4, and the 0-5 Titans improve to 1-5.
Following such a brutal loss for the Colts, they made a big change, firing general manager Chris Ballard. The 10th year GM was fired, and now the Colts are looking for a new leader of this franchise.

According to Dan Patrick on The Dan Patrick Show, the Colts have reportedly made quite an interesting call already. One source told Patrick that Peyton Manning is a name to watch, as he's already been called about the GM opening.
Colts call Peyton Manning about GM opening after Chris Ballard's firing

"The Colts' first call will be/has been to Peyton Manning. The call will not only get names and suggestions, but the call will explore whether or not Peyton would be interested in a general manager for the Colts as the entry point that would include ownership interest in the Colts," Patrick shared.
"The Colts' first call will be/has been to Peyton Manning." — DP shares what his source has told him. https://t.co/MgTbuJIxhW
— Dan Patrick Show (@dpshow) October 19, 2026
This report from Patrick is a very interesting one, and it's a whole lot more fascinating than simply hearing that the Colts will be calling Manning about the opening.
While there seems to be interest from the Colts in bringing Manning in as the team's general manager, they're also looking to get advice from the Hall of Famer on the GM opening.
But in their pitch to hire Manning, they're rumored to be offering Manning a partial ownership stake in the Colts, which would be quite an interesting situation for the former Colts QB.

Manning is still very much involved in the NFL world and could play a similar role to what Tom Brady is doing right now with the Las Vegas Raiders, acting as a key figure in the front office while also working for FOX on an NFL broadcast.
Taking over GM duties would likely take Manning away from his ESPN work, as he'd need to focus on helping the team out, similar to what Matt Ryan is doing with the Atlanta Falcons.

Either way, regardless of what Manning decides to do, this report from Patrick indicates the Colts still very much place a lot of value on Manning's thoughts, enough to potentially hire him as their new GM after nearly a decade with Ballard in control.

articles.headline: Lord of the Rings Director Says He’s Finally Making His Tintin Sequel
keyFacts: Producer Peter Jackson stated at the Sitges Film Festival that he has written the script for a sequel to The Adventures of Tintin and will direct it as his next film.
Jackson reported that The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum has about two weeks of filming remaining and is scheduled for release on December 17, 2027.
Jackson dismissed rumors that another planned Lord of the Rings film titled The Shadow of the Past is in danger following a corporate merger.
body: Tintin fans have been in the wilderness for quite some time. After the Steven Spielberg-directed The Adventures of Tintin hit theaters in 2011, Spielberg and producer Peter Jackson confirmed that a sequel was on the way. This follow-up was originally promised for sometime in 2014 or 2015, with Jackson directing. Needless to say, that didn’t happen.

Thankfully, Jackson finally gave another update on this long-awaited Tintin sequel. At the Sitges Film Festival (which is dedicated to fantasy, horror, and cult films) in Spain, he reiterated that the movie is still in the works. “We’ve also already written the script for Tintin 2, the second Tintin film. That will be the next film I make,” he said. This backs up what Jackson said in May, when he broke years of silence to confirm a version of the script was done and that he’d be directing the movie.

For those unaware, The Adventures of Tintin is a long-running comic series written and illustrated by Belgian cartoonist Hergé. It originally ran from 1929 to 1976 in France, and followed Tintin, a Belgian reporter accompanied by his dog Snowy. In the 2011 adaptation, Tintin embarks on an adventure to find the treasure of a legendary naval warship, the Unicorn.
Peter Jackson provides updates on The Lord of the Rings projects

Beyond Tintin, Jackson gave some updates on the future of The Lord of the Rings movies. He confirmed that The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum is almost finished filming, with about two weeks of shooting left. He also reiterated that in the scriptwriting stage.

The Hunt for Gollum is the next Lord of the Rings film. It follows Aragorn’s quest to find Gollum on behalf of Gandalf before the events of The Fellowship of the Ring. The movie is being directed by Andy Serkis, who is also returning to play the titular character. It’s set for a Dec. 17, 2027 release.

As for The Shadow of the Past, it will take place 14 years after Frodo leaves Middle-earth to journey to Valinor, as Sam, Merry, and Pippin retrace the first steps of their legendary adventure. Stephen Colbert and Philippa Boyens are developing the script. It was previously reported that the film was in danger after the merger between Paramount and Warner Bros., but Jackson has debunked that rumor.

articles.headline: Social media: How to maximize your privacy (and the top settings to change right now)
keyFacts: TechRadar reported that social media profiles expose users to scammers harvesting personal information for phishing and identity theft.
The UK National Cyber Security Centre advises using platform privacy settings to keep personal information inaccessible to strangers.
Users can reduce security risks by adjusting privacy controls, enabling Two-Factor Authentication, and revoking access for unused connected apps.
body: Your social media profiles are a goldmine for scammers looking to harvest personal information for phishing, social engineering, or identity theft. Between birthday posts and family photos, you’re essentially building a detailed dossier that cybercriminals can weaponize against you.
Here’s the good news: with just a few adjustments, you can dramatically reduce your attack surface without losing the convenience and fun of socializing online.

This article is the fourth in a series of content relating to Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2026, which runs throughout October. The previous articles have covered VPN dark web alerts and free alternatives, VPN protection when using AI, and the benefits of dedicated antivirus over packaged solutions.
Less is more

The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) emphasizes that privacy settings exist for a reason: they keep your personal information “inaccessible to anyone but you.” Their guidance focuses on using each platform’s settings to control who can see your posts, contact you, or find your profile.

Scammers can piece together seemingly harmless details to craft highly convincing, targeted phishing attacks. Even a pet name or tagged location – innocent on their own – can become ammunition for someone trying to impersonate you or guess your security questions.
Platform-by-platform quick hits
Here are the most impactful privacy switches to flip on each major platform:
- Facebook: Set your profile to “Friends only” for posts, limit past posts visibility, disable search engine indexing, and restrict who can look you up using your email address or phone number.

- Instagram: Switch to a private account in Settings > Privacy. This prevents strangers from seeing your posts or stories. Disable activity status, restrict tag approvals, and turn off location sharing on posts.

- Snapchat: Enable “Ghost Mode” in Snap Map settings to hide your location. In Privacy Control, set who can contact you and view your story to “Friends Only.” Review your “Find Friends” settings regularly to control whether your account is suggested to other users.
- TikTok: Go to Privacy settings and toggle “Private Account.” Disable “Suggest your account to others,” restrict direct messages, and set duet/stitch permissions to “Friends” or “Off”.
- YouTube: In Settings > Privacy, mark your channel and subscriptions as private. You can also disable video recommendations showing your watch history and turn off location data on uploaded videos.
Universal security settings
Regardless of which platforms you use, two actions should be at the top of your list:
First, enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) everywhere. Even if someone guesses or steals your password, they can’t get in without the second factor – ideally an authentication app.

Second, audit your connected apps. There may be games, quizzes, and other services logged in that you haven’t touched in years. Head to each platform’s third-party app settings and revoke access for anything unused or unfamiliar.
In summary

Spending just five minutes adjusting these settings across your apps reduces your visibility to bad actors and can help keep your data out of the hands of cybercriminals. You don’t need to delete your accounts or leave social media behind – just be intentional about what you share and who can see it.

body: Crystal Palace defender Chris Richards has issued a grovelling apology to fans after the Eagles’ heavy defeat to rivals Brighton.
The Eagles were thumped 5-0 at the Amex Stadium on Sunday afternoon as they suffered their fourth loss of the season.
Richards waited until Monday before making his first public comments about Palace’s humiliation Getty

Meanwhile, it is the first time Brighton have scored five in the fixture since 1956.
The travelling Palace fans made their feelings known at full time as they booed their side off at the final whistle.
Richards initially headed straight down the tunnel without acknowledging the supporters.
The USA international would later return to the pitch, though, after being urged to do so by teammate Jorgen Strand Larsen.
Richards apology
Richards has now apologised to the fans for his post-match antics in a social media post.
In a message shared via his Instagram story, he wrote: “Palace fans, I’m truly sorry for yesterday’s performance.
“You deserve so much better than what happened and there are no excuses.”
As for the scenes at the final whistle, Richards added: “I also want to apologise for walking off after the game.
“I was emotional and embarrassed with the result – I know how much this club means to all of you.

Richards, who joined the club in 2022, stands to leave at the end of his current contract this summer.
The 26-year-old has made 131 appearances for Palace, scoring five goals from centre-back.
He has also won the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League during his time at Selhurst Park.

articles.headline: TP-Link moves to assemble routers in the US following an import ban
keyFacts: TP-Link signed a letter of intent with Key Tronic to assemble routers in Mississippi as soon as early 2027.
The move follows a federal ban on importing new foreign-made consumer routers due to security risks designated by the FCC.
TP-Link stated that components will still need to be sourced from outside the United States because domestic sources are unavailable.
body: TP-Link moves to assemble routers in the US following an import ban
The company says routers could start rolling off a domestic production line as soon as early 2027.

TP-Link is looking to put routers together in the US after the government banned new foreign-made units from being sold domestically. The company has signed a letter of intent with manufacturer Key Tronic and, pending approval from regulators, TP-Link says stateside assembly of its routers could start at a Mississippi production line as soon as early 2027.

Once things are up and running, Wi-Fi 8 routers are expected to be among the first TP-Link products that Key Tronic assembles. TP-Link claims that the agreement is part of its "long-term effort to accelerate US investment in high-tech manufacturing and job creation, designing and assembling next-generation products for American consumers here on American soil."

The company said it will still have to source components from outside the US. "Many [components] are just not available from a domestic source, and this is not a TP-Link issue," TP-Link's corporate affairs officer Steve Kovsky told PC Mag. "This is an issue for all manufacturers that are trying to onshore manufacturing."

In March, the Federal Communications Commission designated all consumer routers made outside the US as a security risk and banned imports. Retailers were still allowed to sell units that they already had on shelves. In its notice, the FCC said companies could apply for a waiver, but only if they planned to move at least some manufacturing to the US. Several companies have received waivers, though TP-Link is not currently one of them.

body: Melania Trump announced a new task force designed to overhaul the federal government’s approach to women’s health.
It will “improve outcomes in all phases of life” and establishes “a new standard for women’s health in America,” the First Lady said during a Rose Garden ceremony at the White House.
President Trump and his wife signed the executive order together that will create the task force and a National Institutes of Health division focused on women’s health.
He praised his wife’s “extraordinary leadership and skills,” saying the First Lady will “help improve the health of our nation’s women and girls.”
The task force will be led by White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, who recently announced that she is free from breast cancer, and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr.
The task force will hold its first meeting Monday afternoon in the Roosevelt Room at the White House.

The order will direct research funds toward finding cures to diseases that affect women in a disproportionate way; use AI to enhance medical research; accelerate the process of getting therapies from the lab to women; ensure women can afford medical treatment and expand education around women’s health.

articles.headline: AI Cloning Threatens To End Public Playtests For Video Games
keyFacts: Digital Sun moved the first playtest for ReVamp from Steam to Discord to prevent AI cloning.
Developers said Anthropic's Claude Opus can decompile and clone game code quickly, posing a high risk for unreleased games.
Digital Sun stated it hopes to open a public playtest on Steam around January.
body: MoonlighterÂ developer Digital Sun has announced a change of plans over a public beta for its forthcoming “tower defensevania”Â ReVamp, based on the recent spate of games being reverse-engineered and cloned using the latest version of Anthropic’s LLM, Claude Opus. What was once supposed to be a widely accessible playtest build via Steam is now going to be limited to a far smaller number of players through the company’s Discord.

“So many of you signed up forÂ ReVamp‘s first playtest on Steam (thank you!),” begins Digital Sun’s update posted to its X account, “but we’ve decided to start with something more contained on our Discord, with the public playtest coming a bit later.” Why? “We’ve been concerned by the recent news of games being reverse-engineered, cloned and published before the original is even out.”

The issue is Claude Opus 5.5’s ability to decompile a game’s code and then recompile it back again in a way that would previously have taken determined coders months to years to achieve. And concerningly, it does a very good job of it, leading to the current rush of games being reverse-engineered and uploaded to be extremely playable on browsers. This is something Digital Sun is obviously keen to avoid for its Dracula-based base-builder that’s not due out until March of 2027, and just handing over a playable build to the public hasâout of nowhereâbecome an extremely high-risk move.
Weâre keeping ReVampâs first playtest small for now.
Hereâs why. pic.twitter.com/VVBm5hoBeF
— Digital Sun â¨ Wishlist ReVamp! (@DigitalSunGames) October 19, 2026

“To everyone who requested access on Steam: we’re sorry for the change of plans,” says Digital Sun. “We hope to open the public playtest around January.” It adds that you can still sign up for the Discord playtest ahead of October 29.
The statement concludes,
Showing games early is how indies get seen and find the fans who keep us going, so we hope platforms keep strengthening protections for original work.

This captures a very chilling thought, and will no doubt raise questions for hundreds of other studios in similar positions. Last week, Drunken Goddess Reflux developer Alliance Arts said it has cancelled plans for a Next Fest demo as a result of the same tech, and while Steam’s Next Fest (starting later today) is not short on entrants (the number of demos has doubled from March’s event to over 8,000), it does seem like something people are going to have to consider.

A demo is a far smaller slice, of course; larger playtests would appear to be a much more risky prospect. Once they could be made available for a limited period and then pulled. All of a sudden, it’s now a realistic prospect that they could be cloned and made available in some form long before they’re intended to be released.

body: What to know about the Iran war today:

- Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov is due in Tehran on Monday for his first visit since the U.S. launched its . He said he will hold talks "aimed at preventing the return of a large-scale war" in the region.

Saudi investment conference to be postponed amid Houthi attacks
A major Saudi investment conference is set to be postponed, three sources briefed on the matter told the French news agency AFP on Monday, amid repeated by Yemen's .

One source said the event "won't happen on time" and that organizers "won't announce a new date soon." A second source, who confirmed the event would be postponed, told AFP: "Who would be willing to risk flying to Riyadh these days?"

Saudi Arabia's Future Investment Initiative (FII) Institute hosts an annual forum often referred to as "Davos in the desert." The event typically draws foreign leaders and business titans, and this year it is scheduled to be held in Riyadh from Oct. 26 to 29.
The Wall Street Journal reported that the conference would either be held online or postponed.
CBS/AFP
Iran says U.S. responsible for insecurity in Strait of Hormuz

Iran's top diplomat on Monday accused the United States of being responsible for the insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz that has left the nearly-eight month conflict sparked by joint U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran unresolved, despite the cessation of major military operations.

"The war imposed by the United States and the Zionist regime [Israel], combined with the economic blockade [on Iran's ports], constitutes the principal source of insecurity in our region," said Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, echoing many similar statements by himself and other senior Iranian figures.

He made the remark Monday during a joint news conference with his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov, who arrived in Tehran earlier Monday for his first visit since the outbreak of the war, as Russia tries to frame itself as a potential mediator despite close ties with the Iranian regime.

Lavrov was also scheduled to meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during his visit, according to Russia's foreign ministry. The veteran Russian diplomat said Moscow's efforts were "aimed at preventing the return of a large-scale war," with talks between Tehran and Washington at a standstill.
CBS/AFP
Iranian oil minister meets Qatari counterpart

Iran's Acting Oil Minister Hamid Bovard met Qatar's Minister of State for Energy Affairs, Saad Sherida al-Kaabi, in Doha on Monday to discuss energy relations and cooperation between the two countries.
According to Iran's official news agency IRNA, al-Kaabi confirmed the meeting, which focused on bilateral energy ties and opportunities for cooperation.
At least 50 killed in Houthi attack on Yemen government camp

The death toll from a Houthi missile strike on a camp in Yemen's government-controlled Shabwa province rose to 50 on Monday, a government official told the French news agency AFP, after military sources earlier put the toll at more than 30.
The Iran-backed rebels fired ballistic missiles at the al-Alam military camp in the southern province of Shabwa.
"The death toll has risen to at least 50, with more than 100 people injured, some of them in critical condition," said Fahad al-Khalifi, deputy governor of Shabwa.
He added that hospitals in the province were overwhelmed and had been forced to transfer the most seriously wounded to facilities in neighbouring Hadramout and Aden.
CBS/AFP
Houthi rebels kill 20 soldiers, Yemen's Saudi-backed military says
Iran-backed Houthi rebels struck a military camp for government forces in southern Yemen on Monday, killing at least 20 soldiers, two Yemeni military officials said.
The rebels fired ballistic missiles at the al-Alam military camp in the southern province of Shabwa in an attack that left at least two dozen more troops wounded, the officials said.
The military officials with the internationally recognized government of Yemen spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to brief the media.

Yemen's decade-long civil war has intensified and become intertwined with the wider regional conflict sparked by the U.S. war with Iran over the last few months, as the Houthis, considered one of Iran's most potent proxy forces, attacks the government's Saudi backers on their home turf.

Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure, including civilian airports, have killed more than 20 people in recent weeks, and President Trump has said he's considering joining Saudi operations against the rebels. The Houthis have warned that if the U.S. does intervene, it would prompt a "swift and painful" retaliation against U.S. personnel and interests across the region.
CBS/AP
Oil prices ease slightly as Trump softens on Russia, after attacks on ships push crude to near 5-month high
Oil prices were down early Monday, with Brent crude, the international standard, falling 2.5% to $107.16 per barrel and benchmark U.S. crude dropping 2.2% to $96.84 per barrel.

The prices fell after President to put new U.S. sanctions against Russia on hold just days before they were to come into effect, drawing , with the move likely resulting in more energy exports from Russia.
Mr. Trump's decision came not long after he said earlier this month he had reached a in an attempt to bring down elevated U.S. fuel prices ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

But despite Mr. Trump's controversial efforts to ease energy costs for Americans, oil prices have remained much higher compared to before the Iran war, due in large part to the ongoing risks to the supply chain caused by the crisis in the Middle East.
On Friday the price of Brent crude hit nearly $110 a barrel, its highest level since mid-May.
CBS/AP
Attacks continue on vessels in and near Strait of Hormuz
A tug boat traveling near the Strait of Hormuz was struck by two unknown projectiles, a British maritime monitoring agency said Sunday.

The U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center (UKMTO) said in a statement that a tugboat traveling southbound off the coast of the United Arab Emirates "reported being struck by two unknown projectiles."
"The tug has sustained damage but is continuing on its route," the agency said, "one minor casualty has been reported."

Last week saw 10 attacks on commercial vessels in and near the strait, according to the UKMTO, which said October has already become the worst month for attacks on shipping in the strait since the early days of the war in March.
U.S. issues security warning to Americans in the Middle East
The U.S. issued a security alert on Monday urging Americans in the Middle East to "exercise heightened vigilance."

"Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," the statement said.

It added that hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly and that groups backed by Iran may target U.S. interests overseas "or at locations associated with the United States and Americans throughout the world."
At least 20 people, including one American, were killed in one week in October when Houthi rebels attacked Saudi airports.
Russia's foreign minister expected in Iran for talks

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov was expected to pay his first visit to Iran on Monday since the U.S. and Israel sparked the ongoing war with the Islamic Republic by launching joint strikes on Feb. 28.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said Sunday that the two sides would discuss "regional and international developments," while Lavrov said his visit was "aimed at preventing the return of a large-scale war."
Russian President Vladimir Putin told his Iranian counterpart in early October that Moscow was prepared to contribute to mediation efforts.

Iran presented a seven-day ceasefire proposal in late September that called for an end to the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and a return to direct negotiations on Tehran's nuclear program. President Trump rejected the proposal, which Iran says remains on the table.
CBS/AFP
Saudi-led military coalition and Iran-backed Houthis trade strikes as Yemen's civil war intensifies
Conflict raged between the Houthis and the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Iran-backed rebel group on Sunday, as both sides traded strikes.

In Riyadh, where intensifying violence has disrupted life for residents, the landmark Kingdom Centre skyscraper ordered "mandatory" remote working for office tenants until further notice. Although a reason for the order wasn't provided, it followed a security alert and two drone interceptions around the capital city, in addition to a number of attacks by Houthis on Saudi targets in recent weeks.

Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition, which backs the internationally-recognized government in war-wracked Yemen, has launched repeated air raids on regions of the country that Houthis control. One alleged Saudi airstrike in northern Yemen killed at least nine people and wounded 16 others on Sunday, the Houthis' Saba news agency reported.

The coalition said Sunday that two pilots were killed when their helicopter crashed in Najran, near the Yemen border, blaming a "technical malfunction" for the incident. The Houthis said they "downed an Apache helicopter belonging to the Saudi enemy" in the same area.
CBS/AFP
Iran says Hormuz reopening conditions still in place

Iran's foreign minister said Sunday that Tehran's conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have not changed, but that its proposal for a limited ceasefire with the U.S. to reopen the vital waterway remains on the table.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday that Tehran is still reviewing "comments" from the U.S. on the Iranian proposal for a seven-day ceasefire that was first presented in September, but rejected by President Trump.

"If they comply with our conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will reopen on the sixth day, and negotiations will begin on the seventh day," Araghchi said, referring to the timeline proposed by Iran, which calls for the U.S. to lift its naval blockade on Iranian ports and to ease sanctions on the country, among other concessions.
"Our conditions are fair, and if the United States is willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, it can meet them within a few days," Araghchi said.

articles.headline: Jalen Hurts expected to miss rest of 2026 season after blood clots found in lungs
keyFacts: Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the 2026 season after multiple blood clots were discovered in his lungs, according to the Eagles and his agent.
Medical experts stated that Hurts has a very good prognosis, is expected to make a full recovery, and will be treated with blood thinners.
The Eagles will proceed with Tanner McKee at quarterback while Hurts is sidelined from football activities during his medical treatment.
body: Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season, according to multiple reports, after blood clots were found in his lungs.

The Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, issued a joint statement on Monday laying out his updated diagnosis after originally announcing he had a superficial blood clot in his left calf that caused him to miss Week 6. A follow-up scan over the weekend revealed deep vein thrombosis, and he had "bilateral pulmonary emboli," meaning several blood clots were now in his lungs.

The Eagles said Hurts' prognosis is "very good" and that he is expected to make a full recovery. However, he will be treated with blood thinners, which will take him away from football activities until he is off the treatment.
Here is the full statement:

"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition.

"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. "blood thinners"). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.

"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.
"We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."

No clots were found until Hurts was in London. It was initially diagnosed as a superficial blood clot. At that time, doctors advised Hurts not to sleep as a precaution, so he stayed awake for roughly 36 hours prior to the game against the Jaguars, according to reports. Despite not getting any sleep, Hurts started and threw for 220 yards and a touchdown.

It was since discovered that the blood clot was "provoked," meaning that it was caused by Hurts getting cleated in his calf during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. That game took place a week before Philadelphia's game in London.

Hurts traveled to London that week, appearing on that week's injury report with a calf injury on Friday. He was a full practice participant that day and had no injury designation prior to the Eagles' game against the Jaguars. Hurts reportedly went to the hospital the evening prior to Sunday's game.

Philadelphia will move forward with Tanner McKee at quarterback. A 2023 sixth-round pick, McKee made his first start of the season Sunday against the Panthers. He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in a 25-15 loss that dropped the Eagles to 2-4.

Hurts, 28, is in his seventh season with the Eagles, who selected him in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft. During his first six seasons, Hurts earned three Pro Bowl selections and helped lead the Eagles to two NFC titles and a Super Bowl title at the end of the 2024 season. He holds the single-game Super Bowl record for rushing yards by a quarterback (72 against the Chiefs). Hurts is one of just two players (the other being Terrell Davis) to run for three touchdowns in a Super Bowl game.

Hurts was named MVP of Super Bowl LIX after amassing 293 total yards and scoring three total touchdowns in the Eagles' 40-22 win over the Chiefs. Hurts has the highest career completion percentage (73.3%) in Super Bowl history among passers with at least 40 attempts.

articles.headline: Meet the Republican Senate candidate who wants Trump to continue the Iran war
keyFacts: Justin Murphy, a Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in New Jersey, told President Donald Trump to continue the war in Iran during a debate with Sen. Cory Booker.
Murphy said a debate clip of his remarks went viral and boosted his campaign attention and fundraising, helping him raise between $20,000 and $30,000.
While Murphy argued for regime change and patience regarding gas prices, Sen. Cory Booker and several other Republicans criticized the war for raising energy costs.
body: Justin Murphy, Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in New Jersey, wants President Donald Trump to continue the war in Iran , a stark contrast to most other GOP candidates.
“Mr. President, put your cowboy hat on and get out there and kick some a** and get this done and done right,” Murphy said about the conflict during a debate with Sen. Cory Booker (D-NJ).

While several Republican candidates in midterm races have called for an immediate end to the war in Iran, often pointing to high gas prices, Murphy told the Trump administration to “stay the course.” The debate clip has now gone viral, with online accounts clipping the video to “Fortunate Son” by Creedence Clearwater Revival, and several big names in conservative media reposting it.

“Finish that war in a positive manner. We can’t wait halfway through and decide we don’t want to do this anymore,” Murphy said. “The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is a radical terrorist organization that has deprived the Iranian people and the Persian people of their history and of a decent life.”

Murphy, an attorney and former local politician, has more views on clips of that single debate answer than he has dollars in cash on hand. He told the Washington Examiner that he “never anticipated” the viral response to the video, but it has helped give his campaign a boost in attention as he faces an uphill battle against Booker.

“JD Vance tweeted, [former national security adviser] Gen. Michael Flynn retweeted . The views on it, from what I understand now, are in the millions. I never anticipated that. It’s welcome news, a little overwhelming. Our fundraising has benefited greatly from it,” Murphy said, though the Washington Examiner could not independently verify that Vice President JD Vance reposted the video.

Murphy estimated that his campaign had raised between $20,000 to $30,000 in the week following the October debate. Though not millions, that is between double and triple the amount he filed in cash on hand at the end of September.
UNDERDOG REPUBLICAN JUSTIN MURPHY TO FACE CORY BOOKER WITH NEGATIVE BALANCE IN CAMPAIGN ACCOUNT

Murphy won the June Republican primary with negative $23.71 in cash on hand. At the end of the third quarter, he filed $9,578.25 in cash on hand, compared to the over $22.56 million that incumbent Booker, a possible 2028 presidential candidate, had at the end of September.

Murphy joked about the fundraising difference during the debate, saying, “I think my Almighty Creator God has made all currency on this planet allergic to me because it avoids me at everything I do in my life.”
He told the Washington Examiner that there is “probably no question” Booker will out-raise and out-spend his campaign, but that his team is trying to put in ground work to make up the difference.

“We’ve been out on the ground at the grassroots level in all 21 counties. We’ve been on the radio. We’ve got a booming social media viral moment right now that’s getting us millions upon millions of views. We’ve got ground game in major counties, important areas — we have people walking neighborhoods, I go out myself,” Murphy said.

Murphy did not say whether he had heard from the National Republican Senatorial Committee. He is not listed as one of the Senate Leadership Fund’s 2026 candidates. He has not yet heard from the White House after his viral debate moment, although he said his campaign is “working some angles to the White House to try to get their interest in New Jersey .”

“We’re working hard. We light a candle, we don’t curse the darkness. Resources would be nice; we would always love more. But this viral moment is actually giving us, I think, what we need, and we’ll just continue to push.” Murphy said.

Murphy’s race, and his Everest-like climb against three-term incumbent Booker, is listed as a “ solid Democratic ” race by election forecasters. There have been no polls yet in the race, according to 270towin.com, but RealClearPolitics ’s latest Polymarket odds for the race show Booker with 97% odds to win in November.

Elaborating on his answer about the Iran war, Murphy spoke with the Washington Examiner about how he would like to see the Pentagon go the distance in Iran. He argued American politicians have to “get over the fear of uttering the words regime change.”

Murphy said he would like to see the United States “isolate the IRGC” and install Reza Pahlavi, the son of the last Iranian Shah, as a “transitionary political figure” until the Iranian people can democratically elect a leader. He added that the hypothetical “probably doesn’t need military intervention.”
He said he stands by the war to, in part, ensure a non-nuclear Iran for future generations of Americans.

“The threats are daily, and while they’re actively developing ballistic missile technology and enriching uranium far past anything that would be required for civilian or medicinal use, so President Trump is right to do what he’s doing. It’s difficult to make right, tough decisions sometimes,” Murphy said.

While Murphy stands by the war in Iran, many Democratic candidates and several Republicans have called for an end to the conflict due to high energy prices from the volatility in the Strait of Hormuz. The conflict has continually been polled as unpopular among Americans, as respondents worry about prolonged fighting.

Several allies of Trump, including candidates he has endorsed, have called for an immediate end to the war as they face pressure on high prices and against Democratic headwinds: Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers running for Senate in Michigan; Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-IA) running for Senate in Iowa; and Republican Aaron Flint running in Montana’s 1st Congressional District have each called for swift ends to the war.

“Michigan families are struggling with the price of everyday life. Groceries cost too much. You have to bring prices down. The war with Iran needs to end, and end quickly. When it does, energy costs will plummet,” Trump-endorsed Rogers said in a campaign advertisement .

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, U.S. gas prices dipped under $3 for a regular gallon in February 2026, before the U.S. and Israel launched the first joint airstrikes of the year against Iran. In May, prices reached $4.50 per regular gallon, while they now sit around $4.33. Murphy says, “Be patient.”

“The solution is to resolve this war in the right way, keep the Straits of Hormuz from ever having to haunt future generations, and increasing our refining capacity. And we will then have conquered that issue, and we’ll have stable low oil prices for a generation,” Murphy said.
He said Trump is “right to do what he’s doing” and that presidents have to make “tough decisions sometimes.”

“Of course, the president would like very much to live in a peaceful world where gasoline is $2 a gallon. We don’t have that luxury, OK? But we’re going to build that world, and we just have to be patient, have his back, and realize that you know we should worry about the next generation of Americans,” Murphy said.
JON HUSTED ADDS TO REPUBLICAN CHORUS CALLING FOR TRUMP TO END IRAN WAR
But Booker slammed Trump and Murphy from the debate stage on the conflict, calling the decision to go to war “one of the most colossally stupid things” in presidential history.

“This is the kind of yahoo, cowboy foreign policy that has mired us in Middle East war after Middle East war, with false-bravado leaders saying we’re just going to go in there and kick a**,” Booker said in response to Murphy’s viral answer. “You know what that’s done to the Treasury of our country? Eight trillion dollars spent in foreign wars in the Middle East, and none of them have ended well.”

articles.headline: Kenya pastor convicted of ordering parents to starve their children to death
keyFacts: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie and 29 other leaders were convicted of murdering 191 people, mostly children, by starvation.
Authorities stated that over 400 bodies were found in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest where the cult operated.
Mackenzie and other leaders still face additional legal cases involving terrorism, radicalisation, and denying education to children.
body: - Published
The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, has been found guilty of murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.
Mackenzie ordered members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".
His doomsday doctrine said that education was forbidden and modern medicine was considered "evil".
Twenty-nine other leaders of his cult were also convicted of murder. They had all pleaded not guilty, repeatedly insisting that nobody was forced to die.
Mackenzie's former head of security, Enos Amanya Ngala, was initially accused but then entered a plea deal and became a witness for the prosecution.
Mackenzie and other leaders of the cult also face a raft of other legal cases, including for terrorism, radicalisation and denying education to children.
But this is the first time the pastor faced a verdict on the most serious charges of murder.
Authorities said over 400 bodies were found in shallow graves in Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast, where Mackenzie led his followers from across the country.
Seventeen men were hired from the nearby town for the horrifying task of digging up the shallow graves. Some were paid just $8 (Â£6) a day.
"Every grave we found had at least three bodies," James, one of the gravediggers, told the BBC. "Some of the remains were of children as young as a few weeks old."
"We once found 12 bodies of children in a line inside a grave. It was massive, the bodies were arranged like clothes. One on top of another."
Gravediggers described some of the bodies of children as having had their "hands and legs tied and bodies wrapped in bedsheets".

Although many of Mackenzie's followers were from elsewhere in Kenya, some of the remains are of people who were familiar to the community because the people in the cult would often go to nearby Shakahola town for supplies and to fetch water from the River Galana which flows through the town.
"We would sometimes carry people on our motorbikes into the forest," said Salim Karisa, another gravedigger. "But it was so planned and secretive that nobody could tell what was happening inside."

Stephen Mwiti, 48, recounted losing all six of his children to the cult and seeing "many bald women and tens of children" surrounding Mackenzie in his house when he went to confront him. Mackenzie forbade make-up and hairstyles, so told women to shave off their hair or keep it unkempt.
Mwiti's former wife was one of those convicted of murder alongside Mackenzie.
"If I met Pastor Mackenzie today, one of us will have to die," told the BBC.
"All six of my children died in Shakahola forest," Mwiti said, visibly emotional holding a photograph of his family. "I only found and buried the remains of my son Samuel."

"This little thing here was the start of all my misery," Mwiti said as he pointed at a dusty TV and cable box in his home in the coastal town of Malindi, 70km (43 miles) from Shakahola. It was from that TV that Mackenzie's doctrine made it to his home.
The pastor established Good News International Ministries in 2003. Over the next 16 years, the church grew in popularity to draw thousands of followers in the church's branches across Kenya.
His church ran a television station called Times TV which would broadcast his sermons from his church in Malindi.
His End Days sermons included conspiracy theories that described education as "evil", healthcare as "against the doctrine" and digital identity cards as "the mark of the devil".
Mackenzie's son, Dan Paul Mackenzie, said he worked as a cameraperson in the church. "The children would sit at the back, adults in the middle, and everyone would sing worship songs all morning."
The pastor would start his fiery sermons at noon, some of which included "casting out demons".
The main church shut down in 2019 and Paul Mackenzie moved to Shakahola forest, encouraging his devotees to follow him.

Peter Shukrani, 23, says his mother relocated to Shakahola with him at the time. He started going to Mackenzie's church when he was eight years old and described him as his "spiritual father", adding that he would "never say a bad word about him".
When in the forest, Shukrani fell ill and his condition deteriorated because medication was banned.
"My mother would throw away all the medicine I was supposed to take because she believe that only God could heal me," Shukrani said.
The community was described as mud houses scattered across the vast forest. "We lived a quiet normal life, fasting for a few days then having a small meal," Shukrani said.

By March 2023 when the first remains were discovered by local herders, hundreds of people had died. "We would carry someone out of the forest but they were so frail that they would die in our arms," explained Salim Karisa, one of the gravediggers.
Shukrani was one of the men rescued from the forest in March 2023.
He was ill and bed-ridden for weeks until that point, but his condition worsened because his mother would throw away all the medication he needed to recover.
"My mother believed Pastor Mackenzie's doctrine that medicine was evil," Shukrani said.
"I would have died if I wasn't rescued from Shakahola forest."
In the 298 pages detailing the charges against him in the current case, 190 victims of the 191 Mackenzie and his followers are accused of murdering are children.
Many of the bodies are still unidentified, owing to their advanced state of decomposition.
In the court documents, several are referred to as "unknown male child" and identified by the location of their grave and date of their discovery.

Despite the suffering endured by Mackenzie's followers, men, women and children who died due to starvation, strangulation and even being bludgeoned to death, as well as his own suffering, Shukrani believes Mackenzie was "a good person who cares for me".
"Mackenzie didn't force anyone to fast. People made those choices by themselves because of their beliefs," Shukrani said.
"I still love him and he is still my pastor."
In contrast Dan Mackenzie believed his father should be found guilty of murder.
"He was the leader, he was someone who they were looking [up to]. So he is a murderer of mass killing," he said before the verdict was announced.

articles.headline: Star Wars Games Could Get More Interesting As Lucasfilm Looks Beyond The Big Studios
keyFacts: Lucasfilm Games Vice President Douglas Reilly stated that collaborating with independent studios on Star Wars games is an intentional strategy.
Reilly said Lucasfilm Games aims to be flexible in partner selection to produce diverse titles rather than relying only on top publishers.
Arcanaut Studios is currently developing the single-player RPG Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic under director Casey Hudson.
body: This year has seen the launch of two Star Wars games, with each one offering a new take on a galaxy far (far!) away. Bit Reactors' Star Wars Zero Company puts its best XCOM foot forward with an aggressive take on turn-based tactics, while Fuse Games' Star Wars Galactic Racer has been hailed for its superb roguelite racing, slick presentation, and the delightful Biddy Blas . Both games have been well received by critics and fans alike, and Lucasfilm Games has been paying attention to the success these independent studios have achieved.

"It very much is part of the strategy," Lucasfilm Games VP Douglas Reilly said to The Game Business Show . "Obviously, huge AAA games like Battlefront are always going to be an essential part of the strategy. But one of the great things about Star Wars is it has all kinds of other opportunities to tell stories in different genres. The goal has been to find the best partner to bring that experience to life inside the galaxy far, far away. And it doesn’t have to always be AAA; sometimes it can be AA, and it’s really about the experience that we’re delivering and the fantasy we’re fulfilling."
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eA3BrR245mo&pp=0gcJCUMMAYcqIYzv

Reilly added that Lucasfilm Games wants to be more flexible in choosing who it partners with to create more Star Wars titles, and some of those studios will "surprise" people when they're eventually revealed. As Reilly put it, Lucasfilm Games isn't looking for a "top five publisher," but rather teams that can meet their expectations for a high-quality title.

Even if the developer hasn't established a track record yet, having experienced members on staff can help. Fuse Games is a good example: it was founded by former Criterion Games developers who worked on EA's Burnout and Need for Speed series, as well as the two Star Wars: Battlefront games at the publisher.

That's not to say that AAA Star Wars games can't be successful, as the Battlefront series has been hugely popular --controversial lootboxes and all--and as of 2019, they'd sold through 33 million units combined.

Konami has also experienced success in recent years by entrusting the Silent Hill franchise to developers outside of its corporate borders. Between Bloober Team, NeoBards Entertainment, and Screen Burn Interactive, Silent Hill has been on a hot streak over the last couple of years.

As for future Star Wars games , one of the biggest ones in development is the single-player RPG Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic . Like Zero Company and Galactic Racers, it's being produced by a brand-new developer, Arcanaut Studios, under the direction of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and Mass Effect veteran Casey Hudson.

articles.headline: Trump takes border crackdown to deep-red state as shock Senate battle threatens GOP stronghold
keyFacts: President Donald Trump is scheduled to promote his immigration agenda at a rally in Kansas on Monday amid recent federal immigration arrests in the state.
The visit occurs during a competitive Senate race in Kansas between Republican incumbent Senator Roger Marshall and challenger Adam Hamilton that has drawn national attention.
White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis stated that the administration has secured the border and removed millions of individuals, while criticizing Democratic immigration policies.
body: EXCLUSIVE: WICHITA, KANSAS — President Donald Trump is expected to tout his immigration agenda in ruby-red Kansas on Monday, weeks after federal immigration agents made dozens of arrests in the southwestern portion of the state.
Trump is headed to the Sunflower State for a rally just outside of Wichita as a tighter-than-expected Senate race that could determine the balance of power in the upper chamber unfolds.
Fox News Digital has learned that Trump will lean into the policy positions that helped propel him and Republicans to power two years ago.
TRUMP DHS HITS 16 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH 0 RELEASES AT THE BORDER

"President Trump stopped the invasion of our country and delivered Americans the most secure border in American history," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital. "Under the President’s leadership, 3 million illegals have left the United States and zero illegals have been released at the border in seventeen months."
"Meanwhile, radical Democrats want to go back to their extreme open border policies, abolish ICE, and grant amnesty to the illegal aliens they released into our communities," she continued.

The Trump-led Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) have touted a string of arrests and deportations of illegal immigrants in the state over the last several months.
GEORGIA ICE SWEEP NABS OVER 700 CRIMINAL ILLEGAL ALIENS, INCLUDING SEX OFFENDERS, CHILD ABUSERS

According to the White House, among some of the "worst of the worst" who were arrested in the state by federal immigration officers include Omar Israel Hernandez of Mexico, convicted of first-degree murder, Jose Luis Rauda-Diaz of El Salvador, convicted of aggravated robbery and two counts of possession of a weapon, Oscar Sanchez-Corona of Mexico, who had previously been deported for drug offenses, damaging property, and driving under the influence, Greg Chukwuka Orji of Nigeria, convicted of dangerous drugs and possession with intent to distribute fentanyl, and Alberto Estrada of Mexico, convicted of aggravated indecent liberties with a child and rape.

Trump’s rally comes as the race between Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., and megachurch pastor Adam Hamilton has cranked up in a state the president has won by double-digits in the last three presidential cycles and has given Republicans cause for concern in a state where voters haven’t elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century.
The Cook Political Report, a nonpartisan race ranker, downgraded the contest to a toss-up earlier this month and money from GOP and Democratic groups is flowing into the state.
KANSAS DEMOCRAT BEGS KAMALA HARRIS NOT TO CAMPAIGN WITH HIM, ‘PLEASE DO NOT COME TO MY STATE’

Marshall, who is vying for a second term, has run close to Trump, rarely breaking from him on key issues throughout this cycle. Trump’s appearance in the state also follows ICE’s three-day sweep in Southwest Kansas last month, dubbed "Operation Safe Community — Kansas," where agents made over 100 arrests.
Marshall pushed back on the operation, demanding that "when ICE operates in Kansas, it needs to coordinate with our local law enforcement."
"Our sheriffs and police know these communities better than anyone, and working together keeps officers and residents safe," Marshall said on X.
Meanwhile, Republicans have targeted Hamilton for his immigration stance, accusing him through ads run by outside groups, like the Senate Leadership Fund, of supporting mass amnesty.

Hamilton, however, pushed back on the Biden administration’s immigration policies and told the Johnson County Post that the previous administration's open border policies "caused a different kind of chaos."
"Record crossings overwhelmed communities, and the immigration courts fell years behind," Hamilton said. "I’m not for open borders, and dangerous criminals don’t belong here."

articles.headline: Uefa gives Infantino two-week deadline to release key documents
keyFacts: Uefa gave Fifa a November 2 deadline to release key governance and decision-making documents.

body: - Published
European governing body Uefa has told Fifa it must release key documents relating to its governance and decision-making by a deadline of 2 November.
At the Fifa Council on Thursday, president Gianni Infantino apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan - but failed to release documents relating to the proposal.
In a letter seen by BBC Sport, Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis said that world football's governing body had failed to address "a number of fundamental questions".
"Any refusal to disclose information or documents should be justified individually, with a clear explanation of the specific grounds relied upon," the letter added.
